summary: Boundary County, ID 20-foot pole tower with L-4 cab built 1937 for Kaniksu National Forest; destroyed in the 1950s; no source describes the site now.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in the 1950s; no source describes what remains at the site

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts labels the site hike-in

events.note: 20-foot pole tower with L-4 cab; both pages give 1937
Destroyed in the 1950s; both pages give only the decade, so no exact year is shown

evidence.supports: Built 1937 as a 20-foot pole L-4 tower on the southwest point of Tungston Mountain; destroyed in the 1950s
evidence.quote: 1937: 20' pole L-4 tower atop southwest point of Tungston Mtn. Destroyed 1950s.

evidence.supports: Design: pole tower with L-4 cab
Location, eight miles southwest of Eastport
No road system like today's in the twenties and thirties; most lookouts built then
evidence.quote: In the twenties and thirties, when most of the fire lookout towers were first constructed around here, there was no road system like we have today.

evidence.supports: Trails from the valley bottom led to the peaks
evidence.quote: Trails from the valley bottom led to the various peaks.

corrections.why: Both pages say the 1950s; neither gives 1950

sources.title: Fire Lookouts of Boundary County, Idaho

notes_for_editor: firelookout.com places the tower on the southwest point of Tungston Mtn, but the record uses the Bethlehem Mountain name and coordinates (48.90021, -116.28798). Check which peak the pin is on before publishing. The brief's 1950 event is corrected to the 1950s. Naturally North Idaho is a local history post used only for trail-era context; it does not name the tower's trail.
